parameters.content:
## Commodity sample quality approvals

### Who's it for
Trading desks, sample rooms and quality teams in agri-food and soft commodities, where the approval decision currently lives in email, chat photographs and a spreadsheet nobody trusts.

### How it works
A dispatcher fills a form and gets a QR. Whoever receives the sample scans it and logs the arrival. A grader replies in chat with a photo of the grading sheet or the readings typed out, and a model turns that into named values. A Code node compares those values against the contract specification, and a named person approves or rejects. Every step lands in an append-only log.

### How to set up
1. Create four tables, or a spreadsheet with four tabs: register, spec, log, counterparties.
2. Put your quality parameters in the spec store, one row per parameter.
3. Fill the table ids and the chat id in the Configuration node of each flow.
4. Attach a chat credential and a model credential. A mail credential only if you want the QR emailed too.
5. Enable the chat trigger last. It ships disabled because enabling it repoints your bot webhook.

### Requirements
n8n 1.60 or later, a chat bot token, and a model credential. Data Tables need no credential, so the workflow runs the moment you import it.

---

**The model reads. It does not decide.** The verdict is fixed rules against thresholds you typed into the spec store.

**This is a commercial quality decision, not a certificate of analysis.** It does not replace an accredited laboratory result or an independent survey.

---

Automatiqa Lab by Aleks Sidorecs
Detailed workflow description lives here: https://www.automatiqa.io/sample-trail/

### Dispatch

A form on a phone, an id, and a QR that opens the arrival form. No scanner, no app, no hardware.

A contract with no spec rows halts here and says so. Nothing is ever judged against a default spec.

**Every storage point asks the same question first: which store is configured?** A `workbook_id` in Configuration means Excel 365, a `spreadsheet_id` means Google Sheets, neither means n8n Data Tables. Data Tables need no credential, which is why the unconfigured path is the one that works. Connect a spreadsheet later by putting its id in Configuration. That is the whole migration.

### Register and send

The register row is written before anything is sent, so a sample that reached somebody always exists on the record.

The QR encodes the arrival form URL with the id already in it. Mail is optional and sits off the main line, so a mail credential you never attach costs you nothing here.

### Arrival

The QR opens this form with the id already filled in.

An id nobody dispatched is refused rather than registered late. A sample that arrives twice keeps its first arrival time, because the clock is a commercial fact and it should not restart because somebody scanned again.

### The clock starts

Arrival is what starts the deadline, so it is computed here and stored, never recomputed later from whatever the clock says at read time.

**Do not remove the sample id from the message this sends.** The grader replies to it, and that reply is what binds an assessment to a sample. No session state, no commands to remember.

### Intake

Everything the bot receives arrives here: a reply carrying a reading, a command, or a button press from a verdict card.

The chat trigger ships **disabled**, because enabling it repoints your bot webhook onto this workflow. The webhook beside it takes the same payload, so you can test the flow before you hand it your bot.

### Your parameters, not ours

The spec store holds **one row per quality parameter**, not one row per contract:

`param, label, unit, check, direction, threshold, values, tolerance_pct, required`

Two kinds of check cover a quality clause. **numeric** is a value against a threshold in one direction: moisture at most 12.0, protein at least 11.5. **absent** is a condition that must not be present at all, and no tolerance applies to something a contract excludes by name.

**Adding a parameter is a row. It is never a change to a node.**

### The model reads

A voice note, a photographed grading sheet or a typed message goes in. Named values with a confidence on each come out. That is the whole job.

The prompt is generated from your spec rows, so the model is asked for exactly the parameters your contract states and nothing else.

Voice needs a transcription endpoint, which is a separate service from the one that reads the text. Leave `transcription_url` blank and the workflow says so and asks for a photo, rather than guessing at a recording it cannot hear.

### It does not decide

**The verdict is the Code node at the front of this lane: fixed rules, compared against thresholds somebody typed into the spec store.** A rejected lot is a commercial argument, so it has to reason identically every time.

The engine has no clock, no random source and no network. Give it the same reading and the same spec and it returns the same verdict, in the same order, a year later. **Swap the model and the verdicts do not move.**

### The gate

The human gate. Nothing before this point decides anything, and nothing after it is reached without a press.

Pressing twice is harmless. The second press finds a decision already there and answers with who made the first one.

### The record

The decision, the handle of whoever pressed the button, and a line in the log.

The decider name comes off the button press, never off anything typed. A name somebody can type is a name somebody can type wrong.

### Chase

A sample that arrived and was never assessed breaks nothing. It just sits there, which is the problem.

Day one nudges whoever has it. Day two goes over their head. Monday brings a digest: what moved, how long decisions took, what is stuck.

### The note

The button on the verdict card is the decision. This form is what follows it: a covering note.

That ordering is the safety mechanism. The decision is written the moment somebody presses a button, so an abandoned form leaves a decided sample rather than a sample in limbo.

### The notice

The only thing in the whole workflow that reaches a counterparty, and it goes only after a person has read the text and pressed Submit. A mis-tap tells nobody.

The text is assembled from the verdict reasons by fixed rules and not drafted by a model, because identical facts should reach a shipper as an identical sentence. The disclaimer from Configuration is appended to every notice that leaves.

No counterparty on file? The note is still recorded and the form says nobody was told. A missing address must never block a decision.
